hypothesis: The remaining first post-write beam difference reflects CPU bus timing and persists into later straight-line reads.
competitor: Only the first beam value is sampled differently; later independent reads agree without persistent CPU timing drift.
test: 32 master-pre-enabled ROM cases with real COPJMP/inert writes, four phases/four repeats, and three consecutive VHPOSR reads before any RAM store. Prefix through first read unchanged from kind113. Two independent A500 captures.

outcomes.multiple reads retain the phase differen: Trace first divergent request/grant; change arbitration, not beam lookup.
outcomes.only first read differs: Investigate the first read sampling/pipeline boundary.
outcomes.reads reconverge after stalls: Use raw slot profiles to identify compensating grants; do not align outputs.

next_question: Does the post-write difference persist through a straight-line read triplet?

hardware.limitations: PAL A500 stock68000,512KiB chip/512KiB slow; silicon revisions unconfirmed. Settled collision truth table, manual sprite0, no Copper/blitter/sprite DMA. DPF pairs otherwise identical. Input and read brackets retained; no trace alignment.
